بعد دعوة السيسي لتفويض برلماني، ما حدود الدور العسكري المصري المحتمل دعماً للسعودية؟. أعادت التحركات المصرية الأخيرة طرح تساؤلات بشأن طبيعة الدعم الذي يمكن أن تقدمه القاهرة للرياض وحدود أي مشاركة عسكرية محتملة، وما إذا كانت تمثّل تحولاً في السياسة المصرية أم امتداداً لمواقف سابقة تجاه أمن دول الخليج.

تونس: ما دلالات اتساع دائرة الرافضين لسياسات الرئيس قيس سعيّد؟. تظاهر آلاف التونسيين في العاصمة تونس، السبت 17 أكتوبر/تشرين الأول، احتجاجا على غلاء المعيشة وتدهور الخدمات العامة، وللمطالبة باستعادة الديمقراطية واحترام الحريات.
من هم أبرز أطراف الصراع في اليمن، وما الدول التي تدعمهم؟. يعاني اليمن من حرب أهلية مستمرة منذ 12 عاما، بدأت مع سيطرة الحوثيين على العاصمة صنعاء، مما دفع تحالفاً عسكرياً تقوده السعودية إلى التدخل.

كيف تتحول احتجاجات جيل زد إلى "كرة ثلج" تهز الحكومات؟. شهدت دول عدة احتجاجات قادها شباب من جيل زد، بدأت بمطالب تتعلق بالتعليم والخدمات والوظائف، قبل أن تتسع في بعض البلدان إلى المطالبة برحيل الحكومات، فكيف أثّرت هذه الاحتجاجات وما التغييرات التي أحدثتها؟

تهديد إيراني باستهداف كابلات الإنترنت البحرية، فماذا نعرف عنها؟. لم تعد المواجهة في مضيق هرمز مقتصرة على ناقلات النفط وحركة الملاحة البحرية، إذ امتد الجدل إلى البنية التحتية الرقمية، بعدما أثارت تصريحات لمسؤولين إيرانيين بشأن استهداف كابلات الإنترنت البحرية ومراكز البيانات اهتماماً واسعاً

لماذا نعتبر بعض الأطعمة مألوفة ونستغرب أطعمة أخرى؟. تختلف عادات الطعام في منطقة شمال افريقيا والشرق الأوسط بشكل لافت. فما الذي يحدد ما نراه طعاما مألوفا أو غريبا؟ وكيف تشكلت أذواقنا الغذائية عبر التاريخ والثقافة والعادات الاجتماعية؟
ألعاب الفيديو.. منظومة تجمع بين وحدة التحكم للهاتف ونظارات الواقع الافتراضي

قصة امرأة تعرضت لاعتداء جنسي في العصور الوسطى وأسرار معركتها القانونية طلباً للعدالة. تكشف وثائق قضائية، تعود إلى القرن الخامس عشر، قصة امرأة تعرّضت لاعتداء جنسي، وقررت خوض معركة قانونية سعياً إلى تحقيق العدالة، فكيف تعامل القضاء معها؟ وما الذي تكشفه قصتها عن مكانة المرأة وحقوقها في مجتمع العصور الوسطى؟
هل تبحث دول الخليج عن مظلة أمنية بديلة عن الضمانات الغربية؟. شهدت منطقة الخليج في الآونة الأخيرة تحركات ديبلوماسية متسارعة نحو بناء تحالفات أمنية ووضع ترتيبات دفاعية جديدة.
ترامب يتهم إيران بالسعي لرفع أسعار النفط قبل انتخابات الكونغرس. هدّد الحرس الثوري الإيراني، باستهداف القواعد الأمريكية المنتشرة في الشرق الأوسط، إذا واصل الجيش الأمريكي مرافقة السفن عبر مضيق هرمز
زلزال بقوة سبع درجات يضرب التبت ويودي بحياة 16 شخصاً. حُدد مركز الزلزال على مسافة نحو 190 كيلومترا إلى شرق ناغتشو وشمال شرقها، و390 كيلومتراً إلى الشمال الشرقي من العاصمة الإقليمية لاسا.

لماذا قد لا تُسفر انتخابات إسرائيل عن فائز واضح؟. في حين يسعى نتنياهو إلى تقديم نفسه بوصفه قائداً قادراً على التعامل مع التحديات الأمنية والإقليمية، يحاول خصومه إقناع الناخبين بأن استمرار حكمه يعني استمرار الانقسامات والأزمات السياسية.

هل يهدّد الذكاء الاصطناعي الوظائف التي تعمل فيها النساء أكثر من غيرها؟. كيف يؤثر الذكاء الاصطناعي في فرص النساء في سوق العمل؟ بين مخاوف الاستغناء عن بعض الوظائف وظهور فرص مهنية جديدة، تكشف دراسات اقتصادية عن تفاوت تأثير هذه التقنيات، ودور التعليم والمهارات الرقمية في تحديد قدرة النساء على مواكبة التحولات.

التحالف يعلن اعتراض صاروخ باليستي باتجاه الرياض ومسيرتين جنوبي المملكة. أعلن التحالف بقيادة السعودية اعتراض صاروخ باليستي باتجاه الرياض ومسيرتين جنوبي المملكة، وسط تصاعد هجمات جماعة أنصار الله على منشآت حيوية، وارتفعت أسعار النفط بأكثر من 1 في المئة بفعل المخاوف من تعطل الإمدادات، فيما أكد صندوق النقد الدولي أن تأثير الهجمات على الاقتصاد السعودي لا يزال محدوداً.

إريتريا.. بلد أفريقي لم يعرف غير رئيس واحد. تتزايد المخاوف في منطقة القرن الأفريقي من حرب جديدة قد تندلع بين إريتريا وإثيوبيا، مع تدهور العلاقات بين الجارتين، لاسيما بعد إعلان رئيس الوزراء الإثيوبي آبي أحمد رغبته في حصول أديس أباب على منفذ على البحر الأحمر عبر إريتريا.

نتنياهو يلغي كل أنشطته الانتخابية عقب إطلاق النار على حاجز عسكري ويأمر "بفرض إغلاق كامل" في الضفة الغربية. أفاد مسعفون بإصابة خمسة إسرائيليين على الأقل، اثنان منهم في حالة حرجة، في هجوم بإطلاق نار بالقرب من مدينة الخليل في الضفة الغربية المحتلة. في حين أعلن الجيش الإسرائيلي أنه قتل منفذَي العملية.

فرنسا تنفي التدخل في حرب الخليج وميزانيتها تروي قصة أخرى – مقال في مودرن دبلوماسي. في جولة الصحف التناقض بين موقف فرنسا المعلن من حرب الخليج وما تكشفه ميزانيتها، ومستقبل رئيسة الوزراء الإيطالية جورجا ميلوني السياسي بعد تجاوز تحديات عديدة، فضلاً عن أسباب انهيار بعض الزيجات بعد عشرين عاماً، وكيف يمكن لعلاقة طويلة أن تفقد مقومات استمرارها رغم سنوات الحب.

فضل شاكر يصالح المسرح مجدداً بعد 14 سنة من الغياب، كيف تفاعل الجمهور مع "عودة الغائب"؟. عاد الفنان اللبناني فضل شاكر إلى المسرح من الرياض بعد غياب دام نحو 14 عاماً، تخللته سنوات من الاعتزال والاختباء والملاحقات القضائية على خلفية أحداث عبرا في لبنان عام 2013. وجاءت عودته بعد إخلاء سبيله ورفع منع السفر عنه

On 9 June, the Presidency announced that President Bola Tinubu had ordered the immediate release of ₦10 billion for Ebola emergency preparedness. Following the discovery of an index case in Abuja, concerns […]

INEC: Results with discrepancies won’t be uploaded on IREV. Dr. Lawrence Bayode, Director, ICT at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), has promised Nigerians that results with discrepancies will not be uploaded to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. Speaking in Abuja when an organisation, RiseNetworks, launched the AI4Election Hackathon initiative, Bayode said any result that does not tally with results on the BVAS would […]

Myths of Battlefield Triumph Are Destroying the U.S. Military. Bad strategy long predates Pete Hegseth and his obsession with “lethality.”
Data Centers in the Crosshairs. Why digital connectivity has become the new front in modern warfare.

Xi’s Gang of Three. How China’s leader divides power between his two most trusted lieutenants.

In India, Rubio Is All Business. The top U.S. diplomat’s three-day trip is focused largely on commercial interests.

Could AI Disinformation Disrupt the Midterms?. The answers are more encouraging than you might think.

Architect of Guards' missiles becomes Iran's defense minister. Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, a sanctioned veteran of Iran's missile industry with ties to the Revolutionary Guards, became defense minister on Sunday, following his predecessor's killing in the war with the United States and Israel.

Iran signals possible nuclear policy shift, threatens US retaliation. Iranian officials raised the possibility of a shift in nuclear policy and threatened retaliation against further US-Israeli attacks, while Tehran outlined its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday.

Trump says US may ‘soon finish the job’ on Iran, Netanyahu vows to topple regime. US President Donald Trump on Sunday warned Washington could “soon finish the job” against Iran unless Tehran changed course, as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel was prepared to strike Iran without US support and vowed to bring down Tehran’s government.

Iran rolls out regional Data Authority amid threats to Mideast tech infrastructure. Iran's parliament speaker said a "Persian Gulf Data Authority" was coming and urged regional governments and investors to withhold resources from AI companies involved in military operations, amid Tehran threats against digital infrastructure across the region.

Retirees protest across Iran over economic hardship, repression. Retirees staged protests in several Iranian cities on Sunday over soaring living costs, inadequate pensions and healthcare problems, with some demonstrators also chanting against government corruption, repression and executions.

US and Israel threaten renewed Iran strikes, Tehran warns of response. US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu escalated threats against Iran on Sunday, and Tehran warned of retaliation even as diplomatic efforts continued over the Strait of Hormuz and the wider conflict.

Soaring medical costs and staff shortages strain Iran’s hospitals. People in Iran have described deteriorating hospital services, rising treatment costs, shortages of medical staff and equipment, and long waits for care, as healthcare workers struggle with low wages and growing workloads, according to accounts shared with Iran International.

Iranians report mass security warnings over social media activity. Iran's police intelligence agency has sent threatening text messages warning citizens of possible prosecution over online activity, including people who do not use social media, according to accounts shared with Iran International.

Teenager killed by gunshot to eye after arrest in Iran, source says. An 18-year-old mechanic was killed by a gunshot to his right eye after being wounded and detained on January 9, according to information obtained by Iran International from a source close to his family.

Iran threatens stronger response to new US attack as Lavrov visits Tehran. Iranian military officials warned of a stronger response to any renewed US attack on Monday, as Russia's foreign minister visited Tehran for talks and regional security concerns grew following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Iranians react to French protests with ‘karma’ and memories of 1979 revolution. Ongoing protests and unrest in France prompted Iranian commenters to revisit the country’s role in the 1979 Islamic Revolution and criticize Western responses to crackdowns in Iran, with many calling the turmoil “karma” in response to an Iran International Instagram question.

Ex-president's remarks expose divide over costs of Iran’s Palestine policy. Former President Mohammad Khatami’s criticism of the costs of Iran’s intervention in Palestinian affairs has fueled debate over Tehran’s policy, with hardliners defending its role and some opponents of the Islamic Republic questioning the motives behind his remarks.

Over a dozen Iranian women and girls killed in 30 days, many by male relatives. At least 15 women and girls have been reported killed across Iran over the past month, many allegedly by husbands, brothers or other male relatives, Iranian news outlet Rokna reported, as legislation aimed at protecting women from violence remains stalled.

Russia vows continued Iran ties as Trump welcomes limits on support. Russia pledged to maintain its political and economic cooperation with Iran during Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's visit to Tehran on Monday, as US President Donald Trump welcomed what he described as limited Russian and Chinese support for Tehran.

Iran deal remains elusive amid risk of renewed strikes. Washington and Tehran may still reach a limited deal, but fundamental disagreements leave open the prospect of renewed escalation, analysts told Iran International, with the period after elections in Israel and the United States emerging as a potential turning point.

Iran’s threats ring out from parliament struggling to meet or connect. Iran’s new defense minister threatened the US and Israel during a parliamentary session held online over fears of attack, but even the virtual meeting faltered when poor internet connections prevented 25 lawmakers from voting on his appointment.

Iran Air chief says 30 to 40 operational aircraft destroyed in war. Between 30 and 40 of Iran’s operational aircraft were destroyed during the war, while another 70 to 80 were hit, Iran Air chief executive Taher Abdolhai said on Monday.

Saudi Arabia should join US-led push for change in Iran, analyst says. Saudi Arabia should join forces with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates to help bring about political change in Iran, rather than continue policies that have failed to contain Tehran's regional influence, an analyst told Iran International.

Iran-Pakistan border trade halt leaves trucks and cargo stranded. Trade between Iran and Pakistan remained suspended at two major border crossings on Tuesday, leaving trucks and cargo stranded, with Pakistani authorities citing security and anti-smuggling measures and Iran pointing to technical difficulties.

Toppling Iran’s regime is ‘primary objective,’ Netanyahu says after US talks. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday that toppling Iran’s regime was Israel’s “primary objective,” a day after discussing Iran with US War Secretary Pete Hegseth during an unannounced visit to Israel.

Pakistani mediator leaves Tehran after Iran doubles down on demands. Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir left Tehran on Tuesday after Iranian leaders reiterated their conditions for negotiations with Washington and ruled out transferring enriched nuclear material abroad, as regional mediators continue efforts to ease the standoff.

Iran in Israeli election: Netanyahu all-in on regime change, rivals want more. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is making regime change in Iran an explicit goal ahead of Israel’s election, while political rivals advocate tough measures against Tehran and criticize his failure to eliminate the Iranian threat.

Iran hardliners split over role of mediators in US tensions. Renewed efforts to avert another war with the United States drew conflicting responses in Tehran, with hardliners questioning mediators’ motives while officials defended keeping diplomatic channels open.

Iran accused of stoking French unrest through influence operations. Iran is seeking to amplify unrest in France through online influence campaigns and alleged links to hard-left groups, The Times reported on Tuesday, citing researchers who accused Tehran and Moscow of exploiting student protests to weaken Western democracies.

Ghalibaf allies seek an end to war without giving up leverage over US. A current within Iran’s conservative establishment associated with Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf favors maintaining military and economic leverage while keeping open the possibility of a negotiated end to the war with the United States.

Iranian women killed by relatives after seeking divorce or refusing marriage. Asking for a divorce, refusing a marriage, speaking to a man she did not know: in Iran, each has preceded the killing of a woman or girl by her own family, according to a Shargh daily investigation that counted at least 38 dead in two months.

Iranian applicants protest German visa delays in Tehran. Iranians seeking German work and vocational-training visas protested outside the German Embassy in Tehran on Tuesday over lengthy delays in securing appointments, with some saying they had already lost job offers or training places while waiting.

IRGC threatens undersea cables, but can it disrupt global internet?. The Revolutionary Guards' threat to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz raises questions about its feasibility, as the waterway carries a fraction of global bandwidth and damaging its cables would not shut down the world's internet.

Land subsidence threatens villages and farms in southeast Iran. Land in parts of Iran’s southeastern Kerman province is sinking by as much as 40 centimeters a year, with ground fissures advancing toward villages, homes and orchards, according to data cited on Wednesday by the semi-official Mehr news agency.

Russia steps between Iran and US, but how far can it go?. Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed Iran with US envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday and offered Moscow’s help, shortly after Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov visited Tehran as Russia seeks a role in efforts to end the Iran-US conflict.

Canada orders Iranian man deported over role in sanctions evasion. Canada's Immigration and Refugee Board has ordered the deportation of an Iranian man living in Toronto over his role in a criminal network that helped Iran evade international sanctions, Global News reported Wednesday, citing a 36-page ruling.

Iran's jailed twin sisters shortlisted for EU's Sakharov Prize. Iranian twin sisters, one sentenced to death and the other to 36 years in prison over January's anti-government protests, have been named among three finalists for the European Parliament's 2026 Sakharov Prize.

US sanctions law firm, shipping operators over Iran trade. The United States on Wednesday sanctioned a law firm, shipping operators and maritime logistics companies accused of helping Iran evade restrictions on its oil and other exports.

Iraq plays down Iran border disruption as more closures reported. Conflicting accounts emerged Wednesday over Iraq's plans for its border with Iran, as Baghdad attributed the closure of one major crossing to technical shortcomings while reports said more could be shut amid US pressure to restrict trade routes with Tehran.

Israel bars United Airlines pilot over alleged Iran links - Ynet. Israel has barred a United Airlines pilot of Iranian descent from serving on flights to the country over unverified social media allegations that he supported Iran's government, the Revolutionary Guards and Hezbollah, Ynet reported Wednesday.

War warnings and talk of diplomacy compete in Tehran. Iranian leaders raised the conditions for negotiations with the United States and issued fresh warnings of a wider military response on Wednesday, even as signs persisted that Tehran was leaving room for diplomacy.

Iran plot suspect says he discussed journalists at London embassy. A man accused of plotting an attack on Iran International journalists told a London court Wednesday that he met an alleged Revolutionary Guards contact at the Iranian embassy while he was gathering information on the journalists.

Iran upholds protester's death sentence over $56 property damage. Iran's Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence of a protester arrested during the 2022 Woman, Life, Freedom movement over an explosion that his lawyer says caused about $56 in property damage, the Emtedad news channel reported Wednesday.

German regulator orders liquidation of Bank Saderat Iran’s Hamburg branch. Germany’s financial regulator BaFin said on Thursday that Bank Saderat Iran’s Hamburg branch had lost its banking license and must be wound up. The branch, which operated in Hamburg and Frankfurt, is no longer allowed to conduct banking business.

US blockade leaves Iran with millions of tons of surplus LPG. Iran's LPG exports have collapsed since the US naval blockade began in mid-July, leaving Tehran to find domestic uses for millions of tons of propane and butane that would normally be sold abroad.

‘Living in despair’: uncertainty, economic turmoil erode hope in Iran. Repeated economic and political crises are eroding Iranians' belief that their lives can improve, with official figures showing declining social capital, widespread perceptions of injustice and deepening distrust of the government.

Iran plot suspect says he was told to break journalist’s arms and legs. A man accused of plotting attacks on Iran International journalists told a London court on Thursday that his Iranian handlers had instructed him to break one journalist’s arms and legs and assault another to stop him from criticizing the Islamic Republic.

China values Iran but won't pay any price to defend it. China regards its relationship with Iran as largely transactional and is not firmly committed to defending the current Iranian government, according to Tong Zhao, a senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.

Iran’s trade squeeze spreads from sea to land. Border closures and transit disruptions involving Pakistan, Iraq and Turkey are raising fears that Iran’s remaining trade routes could be further restricted, deepening the impact of US maritime and air restrictions.

Iran is running out of economic escape routes. Iran faces mounting pressure on its ability to finance trade as a US maritime blockade cuts off oil revenue and cryptocurrency provides only a limited alternative for moving money, former US Treasury official Miad Maleki said in an interview with Iran International.

Istanbul meeting: A new division of labor in the Iran war?. Turkey will host the foreign ministers of seven countries on Friday for talks on the Iran-US war, security in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, developments in Yemen and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Once US blockaded Iran, China’s ‘Malaysian’ oil imports dried up. China's imports of oil recorded as Malaysian have plunged alongside the collapse of Iranian exports under the US naval blockade, suggesting how heavily Iran relied on relabeling its crude for its biggest customer.

Iranian state-linked hackers used US server to target dissidents, researchers say. An Iranian state-sponsored hacking group used command-and-control infrastructure hosted in the United States this year after a months-long pause in operations, according to cybersecurity firm Semperis.

Reform UK donor had ties to Iran supreme leader-linked foundation - Guardian. A billionaire donor to Britain’s Reform UK party was previously involved in a business venture with Astan Quds Razavi, a powerful Iranian religious foundation under the authority of the country’s supreme leader, the Guardian reported.

US signals prolonged Iran standoff as Trump weighs new strikes. The United States is prepared for a prolonged confrontation with Iran and can maintain its blockade on Iranian ports “for the foreseeable future,” US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said, as President Donald Trump weighs whether to resume major strikes after midterm elections.

Massacre au Mali : l’État islamique s’attaque à la communauté idaksahak dans la région de Ménaka. L’attaque terroriste de l’État islamique a coûté la vie à au moins 48 civils dans la région de Ménaka, au Mali. Ce massacre, visant la communauté idaksahak et perpétré en représailles aux opérations militaires, marque une tragique escalade.

En Guinée-Bissau, la junte cherche-t-elle à évincer Embaló ?. Hier soupçonné par l’opposition d’être de mèche avec les putschistes qui l’avaient pourtant renversé, l’ex-président Umaro Sissoco Embaló se retrouve aujourd’hui empêché de regagner Bissau, sur fond de purge parmi ses proches et de report sine die de la présidentielle.

Abidjan-Paris : le tandem Air France-Air Côte d’Ivoire resserre l’étau autour de Corsair. En mutualisant la commercialisation de leurs vols entre Paris et Abidjan, Air France et Air Côte d’Ivoire renforcent leur offre sans ajouter de fréquences. Cette alliance commerciale accentue la pression sur Corsair, seul concurrent direct des deux partenaires sur cette ligne.

Cameroun : comment le schisme entre Nourane Foster et Cabral Libii fragilise le PCRN à Douala. Élue en 2020 sous les couleurs du PCRN de Cabral Libii, Nourane Foster en a claqué la porte fin septembre, entraînant une partie des militants de Douala. À quelques mois des législatives, elle menace désormais son ancien parti dans son fief.

Face à Ethiopian Airlines, le périlleux redressement de Kenya Airways et South African Airways. Dans l’ombre d’Ethiopian Airlines, les deux entreprises suivent des voies contrastées et fragiles vers la viabilité financière, tout en s’efforçant d’attirer des investisseurs stratégiques.

« Le sentimentalisme, c’est fini » : au Burkina Faso, Ibrahim Traoré rétablit la peine de mort. Huit ans après son abolition, la peine de mort a été réintroduite ce mardi dans le code pénal burkinabè. Un virage sécuritaire assumé par la junte au pouvoir, qui y voit un moyen de lutter contre le terrorisme et l’espionnage.

Au Maroc, le gouvernement El Mansouri marque déjà sa différence avec l’ère Akhannouch. À première vue, le programme de Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri s’inscrit dans le prolongement des grands chantiers engagés par Aziz Akhannouch. Mais une lecture croisée des deux déclarations gouvernementales révèle de vrais changements de cap, certains plaçant la nouvelle majorité face à ses propres contradictions.

Avec Somagec, Roger Sahyoun s’impose comme le visage atypique du BTP marocain. Sous la direction de l’ingénieur de 74 ans, Somagec est devenu un géant marocain diversifié dont les activités s’étendent de l’Afrique subsaharienne à l’Amérique du Sud. Pour se développer, il compte sur le marché financier et non sur les banques.

Paul Barril, le « barbouze » français au cœur du génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda. L’ancien du Groupement d’intervention de la gendarmerie nationale français est décédé ce 20 octobre. Reconverti dans le privé en Afrique, il était surtout tristement célèbre sur le continent pour son implication au côté du régime génocidaire rwandais.

Burkina, Mali, Guinée… Le pari de la reprise en main de l’or porte-t-il ses fruits ?. Raffineries, nouvelles règles d’exportation, compagnies minières publiques… Les gouvernements d’Afrique de l’Ouest multiplient les mesures pour reprendre le contrôle de leur filière aurifère. Reste encore à prouver que ces initiatives sont efficaces.

Éthiopie : Abiy Ahmed, la guerre permanente. Couronné du Nobel de la paix en 2019, le Premier ministre éthiopien fait face à une nouvelle escalade militaire. Entre tensions avec l’Érythrée et rebellions internes, il s’enfonce dans une logique de guerre pour maintenir son pouvoir.

Niger : deux otages occidentales libérées en Libye après plus d’un an et demi aux mains de l’État islamique. Détenues au Niger par l’État islamique pendant plus d’un an et demi, Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher ont été libérées et sont arrivées à Benghazi. La médiation a été orchestrée par Saddam Haftar, désireux d’asseoir son influence politique au Sahel.

Affaire Martinez Zogo au Cameroun : Paul Biya a demandé des explications à Joseph Beti Assomo. Le ministre délégué à la Défense a été entendu à la présidence de la République. En cause : des contacts présumés avec des mis en cause dans l’affaire Martinez Zogo. Coulisses.

Mali : les raisons des tensions entre Ismaël Wagué et Sékou Bolly. L’homme d’affaires devenu intermédiaire entre l’État et les groupes armés voit son influence vaciller à Bamako. Derrière ces querelles de cabinet se cachent des rivalités entre généraux, ainsi qu’une féroce bataille pour le contrôle de l’organisation peule Tabital Pulaaku.

Aérien : entre Dakar et Abidjan, quelle porte d’entrée pour le Sahel ?. Sur le papier, le retrait des compagnies occidentales du Sahel devrait profiter à Abidjan et Dakar. Mais le report des voyageurs de Bamako, Niamey et Ouagadougou reste limité, tandis qu’Istanbul, Casablanca et Addis-Abeba captent une partie des flux.

Anndal, le nouveau think tank sahélien qui veut défendre la démocratie. Initié par l’Alliance des démocrates du Sahel, un nouvel institut vient de voir le jour, lequel ambitionne de produire une « boîte à outils » de savoirs et d’expertises pour contrer les discours populistes. Explications.

10 choses à savoir sur Mohamed Ould Abdel Vetah, le « Monsieur pétrole » de Ghazouani. Aux commandes du ministère de l’Énergie et du Pétrole, le dirigeant retrouve un poste qu’il a déjà occupé entre 2016 et 2020. Sa mission ? Remettre sur pied un secteur en pleine tourmente.

Charafat Afilal, une voix qui porte au ministère marocain de l’Énergie. Huit ans après une éviction aussi soudaine que controversée, Charafat Afilal retrouve les fauteuils du gouvernement, avec un portefeuille autrement stratégique que celui qu’elle avait quitté. Portrait d’une camarade du PPS qui connaît les rouages de l’administration autant que les chausse-trappes de la politique marocaine.

Un Français soupçonné d’espionnage arrêté en Guinée équatoriale. Arrêté près du Cameroun, l’ex-militaire français est accusé d’espionnage par la Guinée équatoriale. Malabo affirme avoir tracé des échanges avec un groupe d’opposition classé « terroriste » par les autorités équato-guinéennes.

La France a-t-elle vraiment « imploré » Alger d’augmenter ses livraisons de gaz et de pétrole ?. Alors que certains en France assurent que des « ingérences étrangères » sont responsables des violences commises en marge des manifestations du 27 octobre, une autre rumeur, née sur un site spécialisé, fait la joie de la presse algérienne.

Jusqu’où ira l’expansion des boulangeries Paul en Afrique ?. Après avoir franchi le cap des 100 établissements sur le continent, l’enseigne française prépare son arrivée dans cinq nouveaux marchés d’ici à la fin de 2027. Mais elle doit composer avec une concurrence croissante et des contraintes logistiques, réglementaires et monétaires accrues.

Sénégal : les commissions d’enquête parlementaires de Pastef, outil de reddition des comptes ou théâtralisation politique ?. Sous l’impulsion d’Ousmane Sonko, 11 commissions d’enquête parlementaires ont déjà commencé leurs travaux ou le feront bientôt afin de scruter d’éventuels manquements financiers qui remontent, pour la plupart, à la présidence de Macky Sall. Au risque de transformer l’Assemblée nationale en un tribunal partisan ?

Côte d’Ivoire : pour Alassane Ouattara, les promesses mises à l’épreuve. Un an après sa réélection, en octobre 2025, le chef de l’État a inscrit son quatrième mandat dans le prolongement du précédent. Est-ce suffisant pour répondre aux attentes des Ivoiriens ?

L’opposition algérienne démunie face aux invalidations de candidats aux élections locales de novembre. En Algérie, l’opposition dénonce l’invalidation massive de ses candidats aux locales du 28 novembre. Disqualifiés par la loi électorale et menacés de dissolution en cas de boycott, les partis peinent à bâtir un front uni.

Amea, Infinity, Axian… Le solaire ouest-africain attise les convoitises des géants du secteur. Du Sénégal à la Côte d’Ivoire en passant par le Bénin, les grands énergéticiens avancent leurs pions et multiplient les projets pour conquérir de nouveaux marchés. Un mouvement porté par une demande en électricité qui ne cesse de croître.

Au Maroc, le Sahara fait plus que jamais figure de laboratoire de la régionalisation. La décentralisation est à nouveau au cœur des priorités à Rabat, où le sujet a été remis en tête de la liste des chantiers du gouvernement. Un sujet d’autant plus pressant qu’il conditionne l’avenir du Sahara occidental.

Olivier Bilé, l’universitaire qui veut refonder le Cameroun. Après l’échec de l’Alliance pour une transition pacifique (AFP) à fédérer l’opposition, cet enseignant a lancé Kaïros, un mouvement qui veut réunir civils, militaires et diaspora autour d’une « Table ronde nationale inclusive ». Rencontre.

Mustafa Rawji (Rawbank) : « Notre expérience en RDC est un atout que les nouveaux entrants n’ont pas ». Le patron de la première banque congolaise assume la place du secteur minier dans son portefeuille. Il ambitionne toutefois de prêter davantage à d’autres secteurs de l’économie réelle et détaille sa stratégie pour y parvenir.

RDC : « Vingt ans après la Constitution, il y a de quoi dire et redire », estime Guy Loando Mboyo. Le ministre congolais des Relations avec le Parlement affirme qu’il n’y a pas de projet du gouvernement pour changer la Loi fondamentale, tout en assumant de réfléchir à son adaptation.

Emmanuel Macron annule sa visite prévue au Nigeria et au Sénégal. Selon les informations de Jeune Afrique, Emmanuel Macron, rattrapé par la crise sociale en France, a annulé sa tournée prévue fin octobre au Nigeria et au Sénégal. Une décision qui intervient au moment où Paris cherche à relancer ses relations en Afrique de l’Ouest.

En Algérie, les commentaires non autorisés sur l’économie exposent à des sanctions. La condamnation à quatre ans de prison d’un universitaire pour ses propos sur l’industrie extractive fait suite à la rétrogradation d’un ministre en vue en raison de ses propos dénonçant l’envolée des prix de la tomate.

Soudan : 53 morts après une attaque de l’armée soudanaise contre un marché à la frontière avec le Soudan du Sud. Le bilan pourrait « malheureusement s’alourdir », ont prévenu les autorités locales. Dimanche et lundi, plusieurs frappes au Soudan avaient fait près de 100 morts dans des zones aux mains des paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide.

Se laisser mourir de faim pour « rencontrer Jésus » : au Kenya, le gourou Paul Mackenzie reconnu coupable du meurtre de 190 enfants. Après treize mois d’audience, et l’audition de plus de 120 témoins, le premier procès du pasteur autoproclamé, accusé de l’une des pires tragédies de l’histoire du pays, s’est achevé lundi 19 octobre. Le prononcé de la peine aura lieu ultérieurement.

Madagascar, nouvelle terre de recrutement et d’influence pour la Russie. « Madagascar, un an après le coup d’Etat » (4/4). Mi-août, la mort sur le front ukrainien d’un Malgache enrôlé par l’armée russe a mis en lumière la discrète campagne de recrutement militaire sur la Grande Ile. Depuis l’arrivée du colonel Randrianirina, le pays a entamé un rapprochement généralisé avec la Russie, au grand dam de Paris.

Au Kenya, un gourou est reconnu coupable du meurtre de 190 enfants. Le pasteur autoproclamé Paul Nthenge Mackenzie prônait de jeûner jusqu’à la mort pour « rencontrer Jésus ». Il est reconnu coupable de la mort de 191 fidèles.

En Egypte, le président assure qu’il quittera le pouvoir en 2030, mais œuvre à la pérennité de son régime militaire. Dans deux discours prononcés la semaine du 12 octobre, Abdel Fattah Al-Sissi, au pouvoir depuis 2013, a annoncé qu’il ne briguerait pas de quatrième mandat. D’ici à 2030, il veillera toutefois à ce que ses éventuels successeurs soient sélectionnés et formés par la hiérarchie militaire.

La ratification par la Libye d’un accord maritime avec la Turquie redessine les lignes régionales. Le vote par le Parlement, basé à Benghazi, d’un accord turco-libyen de délimitation des zones économiques exclusives promet de causer des frictions avec l’Egypte et la Grèce, hostiles à cet arrangement.

La junte du Burkina Faso rétablit la peine de mort. Le régime militaire avait annoncé officiellement son intention de rétablir la peine de mort en adoptant un projet de loi en décembre dernier. Elle avait été abolie en 2018.

La guerre entre l’Etat islamique et Al-Qaida prend de l’ampleur au Sahel. Dans le conflit territorial et idéologique qui oppose les deux organisations djihadistes sahéliennes depuis 2019 dans cette zone frontalière, à cheval sur le Mali, le Burkina Faso et le Niger, l’épisode sanglant du 9 octobre pourrait être le plus meurtrier.

Paul Barril, ancien gendarme de l’Elysée devenu sulfureux mercenaire, est mort. Ancien numéro un du GIGN, il avait par ailleurs assuré la sécurité privée de plusieurs chefs d’Etat africains. Au cœur de la « Françafrique », il joua un rôle complexe pendant le génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda. Il s’est éteint à l’âge de 80 ans, a-t-on appris mercredi.

A Madagascar, « l’épidémie de VIH explose ». Le nombre de personnes séropositives a plus que doublé en l’espace de deux ans sur la Grande Ile. Une augmentation d’autant plus inquiétante que le nombre d’individus infectés est sous-évalué, car le dépistage est encore lacunaire dans le pays.

Le Nigeria confirme que son premier cas de maladie à virus Ebola vient de l’espèce Bundibugyo. Cette fièvre hémorragique virale mortelle s’est depuis propagée à plusieurs pays du continent dont l’Ouganda, voisin de la République démocratique du Congo.

Nigeria : un premier cas de maladie à virus Ebola identifié et en isolement. « La patiente, une femme récemment arrivée au Nigeria à bord d’un vol international en provenance d’Ouganda, a été admise dans un hôpital privé [de la capitale, Abuja] », a annoncé le ministre de la santé nigérian, Muhammad Ali Pate.

L’Ouganda, pilier de la reconquête diplomatique d’Israël en Afrique. Le président Yoweri Museveni, au pouvoir depuis 1986, assume son parti pris en faveur de l’Etat hébreu, désormais premier partenaire de l’armée ougandaise.

Chérif Ould Taher, le sulfureux intermédiaire malien derrière les dernières libérations d’otages au Sahel. Enlevées en 2025 par l’Etat islamique au Sahel, une Suissesse et une Autrichienne ont été libérées mercredi. Comme pour un Américain, en août, cet homme d’affaires, considéré comme l’un des principaux narcotrafiquants dans le nord du Mali, a joué un rôle clé.

« Commerçants, femmes, enfants… ils n’ont épargné personne » : plus de 150 civils tués dans une frappe de drone à la frontière entre le Soudan et le Soudan du Sud. Les forces armées soudanaises sont suspectées d’avoir visé un marché transfrontalier bondé de civils, lundi 19 octobre, dans une zone où leurs adversaires, les Forces de soutien rapide, se ravitaillent.

En Tunisie, l’armée tente de ramener les jeunes vers le service national. Longtemps exemptés d’effectuer leur service militaire, les jeunes tunisiens sont rappelés sous les drapeaux par les autorités, qui engagent désormais des poursuites contre les resquilleurs. Des tentatives de recrutements qui s’inscrivent dans un élan de modernisation, mais surtout, de renforcement de l’armée.

Ebola : l’Afrique confrontée à une situation « plus complexe » après la propagation du virus au Nigeria, s’alarme le directeur régional de l’OMS. Au Nigeria, les autorités ont annoncé, mardi, le premier cas de maladie à virus d’Ebola, une diplomate arrivée à Abuja à bord d’un vol en provenance d’Ouganda. Elles ont également identifié 44 cas contacts.

En Guinée-Bissau, un essai clinique sur des nourrissons en partie financé par les Etats-Unis, jugé « contraire à l’éthique », finalement interdit. Proposé par des chercheurs danois et encouragé par le gouvernement américain, l’essai clinique voulait inoculer le vaccin contre l’hépatite B à 7 000 nouveau-nés et attendre six semaines pour 7 000 autres.

Flavio Bolsonaro alongside Lucas Pavanato and Nicolas Ferreita at the rally in Sao Paulo, 18 October 2026 (Alexandre Meneghini/Reuters) (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); A Pew study published in June found that 52 percent of Brazilians have a negative view of Israel to just 33 percent positive. Flavio is narrowly ahead in the polls and favoured by the betting markets. A victory on Sunday would add Latin America's largest country to a remarkable string of regional advances for the US, Israel and the regional far-right. Latin America's lurch to the right Less than 18 months ago, the region looked very different. In July 2025, 30 states were convened by the Hague Group , an international bloc formed to coordinate legal and diplomatic action in solidarity with Palestine, in the Colombian capital Bogota. Thirteen states committed to six immediate measures targeting military exports to Israel and other forms of cooperation and support for Israeli occupation and the genocide in Gaza. ‘Hereness’: What the forgotten history of Jewish anti-Zionism can teach us today Submitted by Fleur Hargreaves on Thu, 10/22/2026 - 10:24 As Zionism and Judaism are conflated by supporters of Israel, anti-Zionist Jews are rediscovering a radical Jewish tradition of opposing it An election poster of the General Jewish Labour Bund reading "Where we live, there is our country!" hung in Kiev, 1917 (Wikimedia Commons) Off British Prime Minister Andy Burnham ruled out a coalition with the Green Party last week after its members passed a motion declaring that “Zionism is racism”, on the grounds that the party is antisemitic. The motion argues that Zionism, the ideology behind Israel’s creation, is rooted in colonisation and Jewish ethnic supremacy over Palestinians , positioning the party in opposition to it. Green Party leader Zack Polanski did not vote on the motion due to certain amendments that failed to pass but describes himself as an anti-Zionist Jew. He hit back in a post on X, calling Burnham “a Prime Minister who arms a genocide and locks pensioners up for opposing it” and accusing him of “the dangerous & irresponsible blurring of challenging Israel & Antisemitism”. Zionism was a fringe ideology for much of Judaism's modern history, only becoming mainstream in Jewish communities and institutions within the past 75 years. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Nevertheless, defenders of Israel routinely conflate Judaism and Zionism to tar critics of Israel as antisemites, erasing the Jewish identity of anti-Zionists such as Polanski and perpetuating the antisemitic notion that Jewish people are monolithic and singularly invested in the Israeli state. While most British Jews still identify as Zionists, younger generations are increasingly distancing themselves from the label. The trend is more pronounced among American Jews - only a third of whom identify as Zionists. Those aged 18-34 are the most likely to describe themselves as anti-Zionist or non-Zionist. Many of these Jews are uncovering a forgotten history of Jewish anti-Zionism and encountering Jewish identities that could once again become a dominant force within the community. The Bund movement When Zionism emerged in the 1880s and 90s, it faced opposition from wide sections of Jewish society, particularly among the Bundists . Founded in Eastern Europe in the late 19th century, the Jewish Labour Bund was a socialist workers’ movement committed to preserving Jewish cultural identity, or Diaspora Nationalism , alongside a broader internationalist class struggle to emancipate workers from capitalism. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); By the beginning of the 20th century, it was the largest and best-organised Jewish party in Eastern Europe, claiming 34,000 members across 274 branches. Molly Crabapple’s recent book, Here Where We Live Is Our Country , traces her family’s Bundist history, and has received widespread acclaim from Jews and non-Jews interested in this past. How the UN declared Zionism a form of racism - Britain then lobbied against revoking the resolution Read More » “As American Jews turn away from Zionism, they are seeking these … liberatory, solidaristic and universalist histories which are so present in our story,” Crabapple told Middle East Eye. A central tenet of Bundism, particularly after the Holocaust, was the concept of “hereness” - or “doikayt” in Yiddish - opposing the Zionist notion that Jewish safety depended on an ethnostate halfway across the world. “Zionism has always been a movement that gave into antisemitic European logic,” Crabapple continued, submitting to the “European ethnonationalist idea that Jews are foreigners who belong elsewhere”. Her book documents how Zionists collaborated with Poland’s antisemitic government in the late 1930s, which armed, trained and funded Zionist militias in Palestine and armed youth militias in Poland that murdered Jews. Arthur Balfour, namesake of the 1917 Balfour Declaration establishing Israel as a “Jewish national home”, described Zionism as a “serious effort to mitigate the age-old miseries created for western civilisation by the presence in its midst of a body [Jewish people] which is too long regarded as alien and even hostile, but which it was equally unable to expel or absorb”. Edwin Montagu, the only Jewish member of the British Cabinet in 1917, was also the sole member opposing the declaration, predicting that it would “prove a rallying ground for antisemites in every country in the world”. For non-Zionist Eastern European Jews facing antisemitism in the 20th century, doikayt articulated “a commitment to worldmaking in the places where Jews lived, called home, [and] belonged for centuries”, explained Miriam Chorley-Schulz, a Holocaust scholar at University of Oregon. “Against Zionism’s settler-colonial solution to the ‘Jewish Question’, this commitment opposed Jewish ‘normalisation’ within racial capitalist structures through ethnostate-building in Palestine, insisting on fighting the material and ideological conditions of oppression here and now instead,” she told MEE. ‘Bundist counterculture’ “Opposition to Zionism was as obvious to the Bund as opposing fascism and any other nationalist violence: Jewish nationalism was just as ugly, just as contemptuous as any other,” Eyshe Beirich, who translated an upcoming collection of Yiddish Bundist writings, We, Traitors , told MEE. As socialists, Bundists organised Jewish trade unions and mass demonstrations with tens of thousands of Jewish workers and students. In Russia , they played a significant role in the revolutions and organised Jewish self-defence during the 1903-1906 pogroms. Bernard Goldstein , the head of the Bund militia in Poland, advocated for armed resistance to Nazi persecution and helped to smuggle weapons ahead of the 1943 Warsaw Ghetto uprising. 'Hyperzionism': How Germany's conflation of antisemitism and anti-Zionism allowed a far-right return Read More » Bundists helped establish the first secular Yiddish school system and institutions giving “education, mutual aid, and organisational support to Jewish workers all over Poland”, Beirich said, building what Jack Jacobs called a “Bundist counterculture”. Yiddish, a European Jewish vernacular spoken by most Jews at the time, was celebrated by the Bund as a secular Jewish language preserving shared culture. For Bundists, Beirich explained, “Yiddish carried the idioms and revolutionary spirit … of the Jewish working class, and it was incumbent on the Bund to support its development.” Although some Zionists supported Yiddish education in Poland, most mainstream Zionist parties opposed the school system, and even collaborated with the Polish government to shut them down, Beirich told MEE. “The Zionist movement eventually opted for an aggressive Hebrew revivalism - a nationalist monolingual project that deliberately suppressed languages spoken by diasporic Jews … as both a tool of negating the diaspora and nation-building in the settler colony,” Chorley-Schulz added. Yiddish, like the Bund itself, was largely destroyed through the Holocaust or assimilation, only surviving in Orthodox or ultra-Orthodox Jewish communities. However, some are now looking to resuscitate both the movement and its language. The conscious pariah Many Jews fleeing Eastern Europe settled in America, bringing “Bundish” ideas which helped build Jewish American socialism during the height of labour organising in the 1880s, joining other immigrants to found mutual aid organisations and celebrate their culture. Benjamin Balthauser’s book, Citizens of the Whole World , revisits the history of the American Jewish left. Among American Jews, there remains a “long memory of a Jewish fight against fascism, nationalism, racism”, Balthauser explained. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); “That was a Bundist idea: that we are proud of our Jewish heritage, of our Jewish identity, but also want to be in solidarity with the working class, with anti-colonial struggles around the world” - including in Palestine. "There is no need for any one of us to serve in the IDF. The IDF should not exist. The state of Israel should not exist." Former Israeli soldier, Meital Yaniv, talks about her experience in the IDF and how it turned her into a peace activist and an anti-Zionist organiser. https://t.co/Zm3jRPzjZe — Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) January 8, 2024 “This memory is coming back … a memory that is buried, but it's a very shallow grave,” Balthauser said, as more American Jews are “remembering this older language, and also realising that this language is not that old”. In his new book, Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History , Benjamin Moser explores past and present Jewish anti-Zionists largely overlooked in an effort to elide Judaism with Zionism. He argued that Jews have traditionally occupied the role Hannah Arendt called the “conscious pariah”, which was part of why they were so often targeted by European elites during times of crisis. Moser told MEE that what tied together these Jewish anti-Zionists across different places and times was that “they are all pariahs, all resistors” who “don’t want to go along with the rationale of power and violence”. Arendt, one of the figures he examines, wrote about Zionism as a means of “getting Jews to disengage from their own societies”, rather than see themselves as interconnected with other oppressed people and the wider working class. Reflecting on Theodor Herzl’s The Jewish State, Arendt wrote in 1946: “Only when we come to see ourselves as part and parcel of a world in which we, like everybody else, are engaged in a struggle against great and sometimes overwhelming odds, and yet with a chance of victory, however small, and with allies, however few… only then will we be able to rid the world of its nightmarish quality.” For anti-Zionist Jews like Moser, the role for these conscious pariahs is now more important than ever. Yemen, Bab al-Mandab and Saudi Arabia: Tehran’s strategic calculus in the balance Submitted by MEE correspondent on Tue, 10/20/2026 - 10:40 The Houthi blockade of the Red Sea benefits Iran but also risks the conflict spiralling beyond its control Commercial vessels are anchored off Yemen's coast at Bab al-Mandab, in the straits connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean on 12 September 2026 (AFP) Off Recent Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and the Yemeni group’s growing leverage over Red Sea shipping have played to Iran 's strategic advantage, increasing pressure on Riyadh and strengthening Tehran’s position in the regional conflict. The Houthis’ capture in September of the strategic Yemeni port city of Mokha from Saudi-backed government forces has placed a vital alternative route for Saudi oil exports through the Bab al-Mandab Strait at risk. For Tehran, this presents an opportunity to drive up oil prices and pressure US President Donald Trump to end the war, while linking threats to shipping through Bab al-Mandab to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. But as Saudi Arabia sought Tehran’s help in containing the Houthis, Iran must also contend with the limits of its influence over the Houthis, who have their own domestic objectives. The escalation has also left Iran facing a delicate balancing act of supporting a key regional ally without allowing the conflict to spiral beyond its control. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); 'Not an Iranian proxy' Tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, officially called Ansar Allah, have been simmering for months. In July, Tehran reportedly sent a plane carrying between 10 and 21 the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) personnel, including senior commanders, to Yemen, according to sources speaking to Reuters, to challenge the Saudi-led blockade. A senior conservative source told Middle East Eye that the Saudi ambassador to Iran, who has a security background, subsequently met Iranian officials in an effort to defuse tensions. Can Iran negotiate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis? Read More » The source said that "Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had signalled his readiness to travel to Saudi Arabia at Riyadh’s request, but the trip did not take place". According to the source, Riyadh wanted Tehran to pressure the Houthis to halt their attacks and threats. Tehran, in turn, called for the Saudi blockade to be lifted and offered to mediate between the warring sides. The source added that Pakistani officials had also repeatedly travelled to Tehran or contacted Araghchi by phone, urging Iran to use its influence to persuade the Houthis to de-escalate. However, a senior source close to the establishment told MEE that Saudi Arabia and Pakistan were mistaken in viewing the Houthis as an Iranian proxy. While Hezbollah in Lebanon could be considered an extension of Iran, the source argued, the Houthis have acted according to their own interests. If the Houthis were simply an Iranian proxy, he said, they would have blocked all ships from passing through the Bab al-Mandab Strait, including American vessels, rather than targeting only Saudi-linked shipping. "Saudi asked Iran to help secure a ceasefire for several weeks, however, Houthies didn't agree," the source added. On 11 October, following two Houthi attacks on Riyadh's main airport that killed 13 people, Araghchi said in a phone call with his Saudi counterpart that Tehran was ready to help initiate talks between Saudi Arabia and Ansar Allah and work toward a political solution to the crisis in Yemen. An unresolved conflict A Saudi affairs analyst writing for a reformist media outlet in Iran argued that the 2022 ceasefire between the Houthis and Riyadh, which largely halted fighting in Yemen, had not resolved the crisis but merely pushed it to the margins. The crisis, he told MEE, had resurfaced at the slightest sign of regional escalation because its underlying causes remained unresolved, while security around the Bab al-Mandab Strait had become increasingly intertwined with developments in the Strait of Hormuz. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); As a result, he added, Yemen’s crisis was evolving from an internal conflict, and later one largely confined to the Arabian Peninsula, into a broader regional and international confrontation. The analyst argued that in addition to immediate security concerns, Riyadh’s insistence on a military approach also stemmed from its view of Yemen as a matter of national and regional prestige and historical credibility. In the analyst’s view, this mindset, coupled with Riyadh’s perception of its eminent role in the Arabian Peninsula, has left Saudi Arabia unwilling to adopt a more flexible approach to Yemen, recognise the Houthis or accept the emergence of a Shia-led government on its border. Sanaa’s new rules of engagement Following the Houthis’ rapid advances along the Red Sea coast and around the Bab al-Mandab Strait, Riyadh turned to Beijing last month for help, as the group’s gains threatened Saudi oil exports and shipping. Iranian sources told Reuters that China had privately urged Tehran to rein in the Houthis to prevent further escalation along vital energy routes on which China depends. Yemen war: Why Egypt's vow to defend Saudi Arabia is a risky gamble Read More » A conservative analyst close to Iran's power centres told MEE that strikes on vital installations deep inside Saudi territory signalled that Sanaa’s response to Saudi Arabia’s actions and blockade against Yemen was moving beyond conventional military retaliation. In recent weeks, the Houthis have attacked Saudi airports several times, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Aiport in Asir province. On 10 October, an attack on King Khalid airport killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300. The following day, another attack ‌on the airport killed one person and wounded nearly a dozen others. The Houthis, the analyst said, were seeking to establish a new set of battlefield equations: “Riyadh for Sanaa”, “airport for airport”, “oil for oil” and “blockade for blockade”. “The phrase ‘Riyadh for Sanaa’ is more than a political slogan,” the analyst added. “It reflects an attempt to redefine the relationship between attack and retaliation, signalling that, according to Sanaa’s leadership, Yemen’s territory will no longer be the only battleground.” The analyst said the military message was inseparable from the political one: Sanaa wanted to demonstrate that continuing the war would carry consequences for Saudi Arabia itself. Tehran faces a big danger A Iranian reformist academic said Iran risks losing its strategic position as regional and international actors move towards a new security arrangement around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. He believes Tehran must therefore seek to ease tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); In July, Saudi Arabia and 13 other countries announced the creation of a maritime military coalition to safeguard freedom of navigation through the three waterways. It reflects an attempt to redefine the relationship between attack and retaliation' - Conservative analyst He noted that what initially appeared to be a campaign focused on countering Houthi attacks on commercial shipping may be evolving into a broader effort to establish a lasting regional maritime security framework, with the Bab el-Mandab Strait at its centre. Countries with different strategic priorities – and, in some cases, competing interests – are increasingly finding common ground around the security of vital maritime routes. This, he added, could have far-reaching implications for global trade and the regional balance of power. "For Tehran, the implications are particularly serious. The challenge is no longer confined to its relationship with the Houthis or its ability to influence events in Yemen,” he said. “It concerns the possibility that a new regional arrangement could gradually constrain Iran’s strategic reach and diminish its influence over one of the world’s most important maritime corridors." The academic’s central concern is that Tehran may be focusing too heavily on immediate tactical calculations while overlooking a much larger transformation unfolding around it. Linked outcomes Iran’s Tasnim News Agency, an outlet affiliated with the IRGC, has argued that the outcome of the US-Iran war and the future of the Strait of Hormuz will directly affect the conflict in Yemen, particularly the strategic balance around the Bab al-Mandab Strait and Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea. Houthi restrictions on Red Sea shipping, combined with disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, have increased pressure on Saudi Arabia’s energy exports. 'The challenge for Iran is a new regional arrangement could gradually constrain its strategic reach...over one of the world’s most important maritime corridors' - Reformist academic “Whatever outcome emerges in the Strait of Hormuz will have a direct impact on the Yemen file, whether positive or negative,” Tasnim wrote, quoting an Iranian expert who warned that weakening the Houthis or ending their control over parts of the Red Sea coastline could have serious consequences for Iran. “If the Houthis are weakened, lose access to the Red Sea and its coastline, or if the United States, the West and Saudi Arabia secure guarantees that Saudi energy infrastructure is no longer threatened from the south, the consequences for Iran could be highly damaging, giving Washington and its allies greater freedom to act against Tehran,” the outlet quoted the expert as saying. Tasnim urged Tehran to step up its diplomatic support for the Houthis, arguing that Iran should not expect its allies to defend it if it fails to support them. "When we do not deploy all our capabilities to defend an ally, we should not expect that ally to deploy all of its capabilities to defend us," the expert said.
