Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs377.71 per litre while HSD will cost Rs391.75 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 23 (Friday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Landslide leaves thousands stranded on Baltistan Road. Passengers cross a road blocked by boulders in the Shangus area of Skardu’s Roundu Valley.—Dawn • GBDMA warns against travel as road to remain closed • Residents call for safety measures on thoroughfare GILGIT: The Baltistan Road was blocked by landslides near Shangus in Skardu’s Roundu Valley on Thursday morning, leaving thousands of passengers, including tourists, stranded on both sides. Local residents have expressed concern over the failure to implement safety measures on the road, which is frequently blocked by landslides and has witnessed numerous fatal accidents. According to a statement issued by the Gilgit-Baltistan Disaster Management Authority (GBDMA), the road was completely blocked and traffic suspended. The authority said debris continued to slide at the site, while large boulders obstructing the road could not be removed using machinery and required blasting. The GBDMA said the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) was mobilising a blasting team to clear the debris. It advised tourists and the general public to avoid non-essential travel on the road, which would remain closed to traffic at least until today (Friday). It also warned people against attempting to cross the landslide zone due to the high risk of further sliding. “The public and travellers are advised to avoid unnecessary travel and contact the police helpline at 15 before setting out to obtain the latest information about road conditions,” the statement said. The 167-kilometre Juglot-Skardu Road, renamed the Baltistan Road, runs along the Indus River and is considered one of the most dangerous mountain routes in the region. Residents of four districts — Skardu, Kharmang, Shigar and Ghanche — depend on it to access other areas. The reconstructed road was inaugurated in 2021. Frequent landslides, a lack of roadside safety barriers and warning signs, inadequate safety instructions and limited telecommunications facilities at checkpoints have added to the risks for motorists. Local residents have repeatedly complained about the failure to introduce adequate safety measures during the road’s reconstruction and alleged that the original project design was not implemented. Residents said several stretches featured sharp turns and were prone to landslides, making them particularly hazardous. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

FIA busts illegal kidney transplant racket in capital; five held. ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has busted an organised gang involved in illegal commercial kidney transplants, arresting five persons, seizing Rs1 million in cash besides freezing properties worth Rs87.5 million and impounding three vehicles. According to a press release issued on Thursday, the FIA, along with Human Organ Transplantation Authority (HOTA), raided a premises in PWD Society, Islamabad, and found that recipient Mohammad Qasim had been transplanted a kidney of donor Ramzan Arshad in violation of law. Three suspects were arrested on the spot while two others were rounded up later. A court granted seven-day physical remand of the suspects. An FIR has been registered under Sections 9, 10 and 11(a)(ii) of the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 2010 read with Sections 34, 419 and 109 of Pakistan Penal Code. Investigations said that the recipient had paid Rs3 million in cash for the transplant. Agents arranged the donor. The agents had promised Rs400,000 to the donor, of which Rs340,000 was to be given to the donor and Rs60,000 to be distributed among three agents as commission. The suspects had been performing transplants in residential houses without any medical degree or certificate. Necessary tissue typing, cross-match, PRA and HLA tests were conducted illegally through a hospital by agents. Since these tests are conducted only for HOTA-approved close relatives, the suspects would submit donor samples under names of recipient’s relatives with fake referral letters to make it appear as a relative donor case. Dialysis of recipients was arranged through a technician of a hospital in Islamabad, while in case of deterioration of condition after transplant, the patient was shifted to another hospital. The network consisted of agents, a doctor, nurse, anaesthesia provider, medicine supplier, laboratory test facilitator and dialysis provider. The gang had been operating at private places in PWD Society, Bahria Phase-4 and Peshawar. Investigations further revealed that the suspects had purchased properties in Islamabad from illicit proceeds of illegal transplants. One of them had purchased a 10-marla house in Media Town, Islamabad, for Rs62.5 million, while another purchased a 5-marla house in Jinnah Garden Phase-I, Islamabad, for Rs25 million. Transfer of both properties has been frozen by issuing notices under Section 5 of the FIA Act, 1974. Letters have been sent to all banks for obtaining records of the suspects and separate money laundering proceedings against both were under consideration. During search, Rs1 million cash was recovered and three vehicles — one Changan Oshan X7 and two Honda Civics — were seized and their transfer and registration frozen through the excise office. Teams from HOTA, Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority (IHRA) and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) inspected the illegal set-up and will submit separate reports. The illegal set-up has been sealed. The operation was conducted on directions of Director FIA Islamabad Zone Syed Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari and under supervision of Deputy Director FIA Anti-Corruption Circle, Islamabad, Faizan Mir. Raids were being conducted at various places for the arrest of the remaining suspects and further investigation was underway. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives. • Rebels claim targeting Saudi defence ministry, Aramco installations, Dammam airport • Coalition downs four drones above Riyadh, Madina • Egypt urges talks as its parliament weighs military backing for Saudi campaign in Yemen • IRGC warns US against escorting ships thru Hormuz • Pakistan warns pilgrims travelling between Iran and Iraq RIYADH: Yemen’s Houthi forces said on Thursday they had launched attacks on Saudi Arabia’s defence ministry in Riyadh, Aramco facilities in Yanbu and the King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, where Saudi authorities said two people were killed. Meanwhile, Iran’s Revolu­tio­nary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. The strike on the airport in the kingdom’s eastern oil hub on Wednesday evening killed a Saudi citizen and an Indian national and wounded eight others, according to Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation. It said the injuries ranged from minor to serious, and that operations had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal. Elsewhere, two people were reportedly killed in a Houthi drone attack on a Saudi oil field. The Saudi-led coalition said separately that it had intercepted and destroyed four drones over the Riyadh and Madina regions. Meanwhile, in a televised speech, the Houthi military spok­es­person, Yahya Saree, claimed attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and on the defence ministry in Riyadh. Saree said Saudi attacks had killed and wounded 562 people in Yemen since mid-July, when the Houthis imposed a naval blockade on the kingdom. The coalition warned at the time that it would respond “firmly”. Following attacks in the region, Aramco told staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran, on the Gulf coast, and work remotely, six people with knowledge of the matter said. Oil prices This would be the company’s first such evacuation since the Iran war began. The Houthis cau­sed extensive damage to the headquarters earlier this month, when a strike on the building sent fire spreading across several floors. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but Saudi Arabia’s benchmark stock index fell 2.5pc on Thursday. Oil prices rose about 3pc to a five-month high. Brent crude fut­ures gained $3.51 to $112.33 a barrel, while US West Texas Inter­mediate rose $2.14 to $99.29. Brent entered technically overbought territory for the third time in a week and is on course for its highest close since 4 May. Analysts said the attacks were outweighing more positive signals on supply. “Reports of Middle East crude oil exports exceeding pre-conflict levels are more than countered by attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and on its oil infrastructure,” said Tamas Varga of PVM Oil. Morgan Stanley estimated that the region’s crude exports ran at about 17m barrels a day last week, compared with an average of about 18m in the 12 months before the war. Egypt urges diplomacy Against this backdrop, Egypt’s foreign minister said Cairo favoured exploring “every opportunity” to resolve the conflict diplomatically, days before a parliamentary vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. Direct involvement by Egypt’s military, one of the region’s largest, would raise the stakes in a front that is increasingly destabilising the wider war. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Saturday for an urgent parliamentary session on the question, but after a closed meeting on Sunday, lawmakers postponed the vote until October 26 to allow further deliberation. On Saturday, Yahya Ali al-Rai, speaker of the Houthi-run House of Representatives, warned against Egyptian involvement and urged parliament to reject the proposal. “Should Egypt slide down this path, it would pose a grave threat to its own national security and internal stability,” he said. Hormuz attacks Meanwhile, the IRGC said on Thursday that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday. The Iranian forces added that three more vessels collided with mines west of the strait, and warned the US military that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against its regional bases. “This is a serious warning,” they added. Warning for pilgrims Separately, Pakistan’s Ministry of Religious Affairs has urged pilgrims to either use Iranian carriers or verify “every Iran-Iraq air sector before departure” when travelling between Iran and Iraq. In a notice, the ministry said it received guidance from the Foreign Office and urged travellers to “use Iranian airlines or plan onward travel between Tehran/Mashad and Najaf” and “verify every Iran-Iraq air sector before departure”. Zaireen group organisers have been instructed to “avoid relying on unconfirmed Iranian connections and to maintain alternative land routes or air arrangements, sufficient contingency funds and accommodation plans in case of cancellations”. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

Peshawar High Court bars arrest of KP Assembly deputy speaker. PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) has restrained the authorities from arresting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Deputy Speaker Suriya Bibi until Nov 10, while allowing her to retain access to her official residence. A bench comprising Justices Ijaz Anwar and Muhammad Faheem Wali ordered that the Oct 14 order to vacate her official residence remain suspended. It also provisionally allowed her to occupy the accommodation until the next hearing. “The respondents are further restrained from arresting the petitioner till the date fixed,” the bench ruled in its three-page order sheet. The court fixed Nov 10 for the next hearing of Ms Bibi’s petition against the sealing of her official residence and her anticipated arrest under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance. Court also allows Suriya Bibi to retain official residence, suspends order to vacate it The bench observed that the proclamation imposing governor’s rule in the province did not mention the speaker or deputy speaker among the functionaries who ceased to hold office. “Apparently, the presidential order does not find mention of the position of speaker/deputy speaker. Similarly, even the vacation order makes reference to those categories (of ministers and advisers) but it nowhere mentions the position of speaker/deputy speaker, which prima facie suggests that the same is not covered by the proclamation order,” it observed. The bench noted that Advocate Gen­eral Sanaullah had argued that in “view of Federal Government Order-1 of 2026, read with Federal Government Order-2 of 2026 and the Oct 11 proclamation” for an emergency, the government had every authority to have official accommodation vacated by advisers and provincial ministers, including the deputy speaker. He also contended that the petitioner had been named in an FIR registered on behalf of the Chitral deputy commissioner on Oct 12 under Section 406 of the Pakistan Penal Code. The bench reproduced the proclamation order regarding the cessation of certain categories of the public representatives. “The chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and the advocate general of the province of KP shall forthwith cease to hold office,” one of its provisions said. The court also referred to arguments by the petitioner’s counsel, Yasir Khattak, who cited Section 8 of the KP Province Speaker and Deputy Speaker’s (Immunities, Privileges, Salaries and Allowances) Act, 2026. It entitles the speaker and deputy speaker to use official accommodation with­out paying rent until they are replaced and their substitutes are chosen. The lawyer also cited Section 27(2) of the act, which provided that the deputy speaker could not be arrested, detained or confined, and that her official residence could not be searched, entered or raided by a law enforcement agency during her term in office. He claimed that after governor’s rule was imposed in the province, pol­ice raided his client’s official residence “without any reason and justification to harass her and unlawfully arrest her”. He added that at midnight on Oct 14, the respondents and other officials again raided the residence and locked it. The petitioner asked the court to direct the provincial government and the ins­pector general of police to immediately unseal her residence and restore her access to and possession of the property. She also sought directions restraining the KP police chief and Peshawar deputy commissioner from raiding her residence or arresting or detaining her under any order issued pursuant to Section 3 of the MPO Ordinance. Following the imposition of governor’s rule, a case was registered against the deputy speaker for allegedly “refusing to return an official vehicle”. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

National Assembly proceedings succumb to lack of quorum, again. • CDA only demolishing illegal structures in Islamabad, assembly told • MNA raises concern over non-rehabilitation of Malir families displaced by ML-1 project • Lower house amends law to make State Life Insurance Company a statutory body ISLAMABAD: Proceedings in the National Assembly remained sluggish on Thursday, with only one bill passed before a lack of quorum forced the presiding officer to adjourn the sitting until Friday morning. The NA’s agenda for Thursday comprised 16 items, but the sitting was adjourned midway after a PTI MNA pointed out the lack of quorum. A headcount confirmed that the required number of members was not present. Abdul Qadir Patel, who was presiding over the sitting, allowed some additional time for the quorum to be completed, but the number of MNAs present remained below the required 88. The House was subsequently adjourned until Friday morning. During the question hour, the demolition of houses and other struc­tures in Islamabad, particularly in Sector E-12, came under discussion. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry said the Capital Development Authority (CDA) had demolished only illegally constructed structures and houses. He said the shortage of graveyards was one of the major problems facing the city’s administration and residents. Most private housing schemes and societies, he added, had converted plots reserved for graveyards, schools, parks and mosques into commercial properties. Responding to a question, Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi informed the House that Pakistan Railways had recovered more than 200,000 kanals of land previously occupied through encroachments. Regarding the Main Line-1 (ML-1) railway project, he said Prime Min­ister Shehbaz Sharif would inau­gurate its first phase, involving the laying of 480 kilometres of railway track between Rohri and Karachi, at an estimated cost of $2.5 billion. MNA Syed Rafiullah said several families in Karachi’s Malir area had been rendered homeless by the ML-1 project, but had yet to be rehabilitated. During a question concerning facilities for Haj pilgrims, PTI MNA Shehryar Afridi expre­ssed displeasure when Parliamentary Secre­tary Kesoo Mal Kheal Das responded to the query. “It would have been better if a responsible member of the treasury benches or the minister for parliamentary affairs had answered the question,” Mr Afridi said. Mr Das responded by pointing out that a Hindu minister in India also handled Haj affairs, questioning Mr Afridi’s suggestion that the matter required a more responsible person to address it. Mr Afridi also said some private Haj organisers had made the religious obligation prohibitively exp­en­sive, with packages costing bet­ween Rs4 million and Rs5m. State Life Insurance Company After Question Hour, the National Assembly passed the Life Insurance (Nation­alisation) (Amend­ment) Bill, 2026. The bill provides for the federal government to establish a company, to be known as State Life Insurance Company Limited, under the Companies Act, 2017 (XIX of 2017). It states that the appointment of the company’s chief executive officer and board of directors will be made in accordance with the State-Owned Enterprises (SOE) Act and the Companies Act, 2017. Following the company’s incorporation under the Companies Act, 2017, the federal government will issue a vesting order, to be published in the official gazette, transferring all assets, liabilities, contracts, policies, proceedings and undertakings of the existing corporation to the company on a specified date and under terms and conditions determined by the government. The corporation will stand dissolved on the effective date, according to the bill. The legislation further provides that all employees and officers who have served the corporation continuously for at least one year immediately before the effective date, excluding those employed under project contracts, will be transferred to the new company on the same terms and conditions of service. Their existing rights and privileges, including pension entitleme­nts, post-retirement medical benefits, provident fund and gratuity, will also be protected, the bill states. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

Three terrorists killed as forces foil attack in Gwadar. GWADAR/QUETTA: Security forces killed three terrorists and foiled an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar, officials said on Thursday. Security sources said forces had surrounded several other suspected terrorists near a hotel, and an operation was underway to thwart another attempted attack. The construction camp that was targeted by terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan was empty, and no casualties were reported, officials said. However, the attackers set fire to several trucks parked along a nearby road, they added. Officials denied reports of attacks on security forces, intelligence agencies and their camps, describing information circulating on social media as baseless, and urged the public not to treat unverified reports and claims circulated by terrorist organisations as established facts. Security situation Meanwhile, in a joint statement, the Gwadar administration and police said reports circulating on social media about the security situation were inaccurate. The law and order situation in the BP-250 area and its surroundings was under control following timely action by security forces and relevant intelligence agencies, the statement said. Gwadar police assured residents that necessary measures were being taken to maintain law and order. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, in a post on X, lauded security forces for thwarting the attack and praised their professionalism in eliminating terrorists. Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026

Tensions with Karachi Metropolitan Corporation flare as railways calls in armed personnel from other cities. • PR police say step taken to protect federal assets following ‘recent incidents’ • Both sides have already lodged cases against each other over scuffle between city wardens and PR policemen KARACHI: In a clear sign of further escalation of tensions between the KMC and Pakistan Railways, the federal institution has called in additional forces from different parts of the country “equipped with arms and ammunition” to protect its assets and key points in Karachi, warning that it will respond with “full force” if any individual or institution challenges its authority. The dispute is the KMC’s Rs780 million road construction project linking Natha Khan Bridge with Pehlwan Goth, as both the federal and municipal authorities claim ownership of the land. The two sides have already lodged cases against each other, accusing one another of serious offences, including terrorism and kidnapping, while senior officials of both institutions have vowed that they would not back down from their respective positions. On Sunday the railways police stopped the construction of the dual carriageway between Natha Khan Bridge and Pehlwan Goth and Habib University, running parallel to Chakor Nullah. The railways maintained that the project encroaches on the land belonging to the Karachi Circular Railway (KCR) and that the construction was without authorisation. A scuffle had also broken out when KMC City Wardens Dire­ctor Saim Imran arrived at the scene, followed by heated arguments between the two sides. The KMC alleged PR policemen assaulted the City Wardens director before taking him to the railways police station. Although the City Wardens director was released after hours of talks between the two sides, the KMC high-ups moved the Sharea Faisal police to lodge an FIR against the PR police officials for kidnapping and assaulting their officer. The matter did not end there, piles of garbage were found the next day outside the PR offices and the residence of one of its senior officials, raising suspicions among the officials that the waste had been dumped by the municipal body’s officials. Later on, a heavy contingent of Sharea Faisal police “raided” the Cantonment Railway Station to arrest suspects allegedly involved in the “kidnapping, torture and illegal confinement” of the KMC City Wardens director. In a tit-for-tat move, the railways lodged an FIR against KMC officials later in the evening, accusing them of offences including terrorism. In a fresh move, Pakistan Railways has decided to call in additional personnel from Sukkur and Multan for deployment in Karachi. It already has a force of more than 500 personnel in the city. In separate letters to senior Pakistan Railways police officials in the two cities, the department has asked them to release a certain number of personnel “along with arms and ammunition” for deployment in Karachi. When contacted, SP Pakistan Railways Police Karachi Khurram Khursheed confirmed the move, saying that the additional force had been called in as a “precautionary measure” following “recent incidents”, including an attack on a railway police station and the dumping of garbage outside railway offices and the residence of one of its senior officials. “The railway police force is usually deployed on trains, at stations, key points, Pakistan Railways offices and the residences of senior officials,” he told Dawn. “The additional personnel will join the existing force to strengthen security. Under its mandate, the railway police are responsible for protecting Pakistan Railways’ assets and key points. We hope the additional deployment will help the force perform its duties more effectively.” Meanwhile, the KMC has continued work on the Natha Khan-Pehalwan Goth road to complete it by the end of this month. “The work was temporarily halted when Pakistan Railways police intervened but it resumed the very next day,” a KMC official said. “Talks between senior officials of the two sides are ongoing but the issue remains unresolved. Pakistan Railways insists that the land belongs to it while the KMC is determined to complete the project without interruption. The KMC has fulfilled all legal requirements before launching the project more than two months ago. This is a major project that will benefit the people and any attempt to undermine its potential or put it at risk would be detrimental to the interests of Karachi’s residents.” Published in Dawn, October 23rd, 2026
